title: LA-Style Galbi
shortDescription: Flanken-cut beef short ribs marinated with Korean pear, soy, onion, garlic, and sesame, then grilled quickly across their thin cut.
culturalContext: LA galbi uses short ribs sliced thinly across several bones. It is strongly associated with Korean-American cooking, but explanations for the name and precise origin vary; this draft avoids presenting any one origin theory as settled fact.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

totalTime.display: 4 hours 45 minutes, including minimum marination and rest

equipment: Nonreactive mixing bowl or food-safe zip bag
Outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric tabletop grill

ingredients.item: flanken-cut beef short ribs, about 6 mm / 1/4 inch thick
ingredients.preparation: ask the butcher to remove bone dust; inspect each strip

marinadeOrSeasoning.meatWeightCovered: 1.5 kg / 3.3 lb flanken-cut beef short ribs
mixOrder: Whisk soy sauce, water, and brown sugar until partly dissolved.
Blend pear, onion, garlic, and ginger until smooth.
Combine the blended mixture with the soy base, sesame oil, and pepper.
marinadeOrSeasoning.marinationVessel: Large nonreactive dish or food-safe zip bags arranged in a single layer on a rimmed tray
marinadeOrSeasoning.maximumPracticalMarinationWarning: Do not exceed 24 hours; thin flanken ribs can become overly soft from pear and overly salty from extended contact.
marinadeOrSeasoning.reserveBeforeRawContactInstruction: Reserve any portion intended for basting or serving before the ribs enter the marinade.
marinadeOrSeasoning.rawContactDiscardOrReboilInstruction: Discard marinade that contacted raw ribs. Do not brush it onto cooked ribs.
substitutions: Ripe Bosc pear may replace Korean pear by weight.
Certified gluten-free tamari may replace soy sauce after full label review.
allergenNotes: Regular soy sauce usually contains wheat.

instructions.heading: Inspect the flanken ribs
instructions.action: Keep ribs cold. Ask the butcher to remove bone dust; inspect each strip and lift off visible fragments with a clean damp disposable towel. Do not rinse the beef.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Each strip is about 6 mm / 1/4 inch thick with no visible loose bone fragments.
instructions.safetyNote: FoodSafety.gov advises against rinsing raw meat because splashing spreads contamination; sanitize contacted surfaces.

instructions.heading: Blend the marinade
instructions.action: Whisk soy sauce, water, and sugar. Blend pear, onion, garlic, and ginger, then combine with the soy base, sesame oil, and pepper.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The marinade is pourable and evenly blended with no large onion pieces.
instructions.safetyNote: Reserve any serving portion before raw ribs are added.

instructions.heading: Marinate flat and cold
instructions.action: Arrange ribs in the vessel, coat every surface, cover, and refrigerate 4 to 12 hours, turning once.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: All strips are submerged or evenly coated without folded dry sections.
instructions.safetyNote: Never marinate on the counter; discard marinade after removing the ribs.

instructions.heading: Preheat and drain
instructions.action: Preheat the approved grill to medium-high. Clean and oil the surface. Lift ribs from marinade and let excess drip off.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The ribs sizzle immediately and lie flat across the grate.
instructions.safetyNote: Use only outdoor grills outdoors or manufacturer-approved indoor electric appliances indoors.

instructions.heading: Grill the ribs
instructions.action: Grill in a single layer for about 2 to 3 minutes per side, moving pieces away from flare-ups and checking the thickest meat between bones.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The surface is caramelized without blackened sugar, and the thickest meat reaches target temperature.
instructions.safetyNote: Avoid touching bone with the thermometer tip; use clean tongs and a clean cooked-food platter.

instructions.heading: Rest, cut, and serve
instructions.action: Rest ribs for at least 3 minutes. Use clean kitchen shears to cut meat into manageable pieces if desired, leaving bones easy to identify.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Juices settle and pieces remain moist; bones are clearly visible for diners.
instructions.safetyNote: Warn children and guests about bone pieces; do not return cooked ribs to the raw vessel.

grillSetup: Preheat a clean outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric tabletop grill to medium-high, about 400–450°F / 204–232°C. Follow the appliance manual for clearance and ventilation; never use charcoal, propane, butane camping stoves, or outdoor grills indoors.
targetInternalTemperature: 145°F / 63°C in the thickest practical portion, followed by a 3-minute rest
visualDonenessCues: Ribs are caramelized at the edges without a charred sugar crust.
The thickest meat between bones reaches 145°F / 63°C and rests 3 minutes.
foodSafetyNotes: Keep raw beef and its marinade separate from ready-to-eat foods; wash hands and sanitize contacted surfaces.
Use separate raw and cooked plates and utensils, or wash and sanitize them fully before reuse.
Measure the thickest practical portion with a calibrated food thermometer; grill marks and time alone do not establish doneness.
For whole-cut beef, reach 145°F / 63°C and rest for at least 3 minutes before serving.
Use only an outdoor grill or an electric tabletop appliance explicitly approved by its manufacturer for indoor use; follow ventilation and clearance instructions.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Check every packaged-ingredient label and prevent cross-contact; substitutions do not guarantee an allergen-free result.

substitutions: Use ripe Bosc pear by weight if Korean pear is unavailable.
Do not replace flanken ribs with thick English-cut ribs without developing a different cooking method and timing.
ingredientSourcing: Request flanken-cut short ribs approximately 6 mm / 1/4 inch thick from a Korean market or butcher.
Ask the butcher to remove bone dust from the saw cut and inspect again at home.
makeAhead: Blend the marinade up to 1 day ahead and refrigerate it before raw contact. Marinate ribs 4 to 12 hours; do not exceed 24 hours.
storage: Refrigerate cooked beef within 2 hours in a shallow airtight container at 40°F / 4°C or below; use within 3 days.
reheating: Reheat leftovers to 165°F / 74°C. Reheat only the portion needed and avoid prolonged cooking that toughens thin beef.
leftovers: Remove meat from bones, reheat to 165°F / 74°C, and use in rice bowls or lettuce wraps. Discard bones and any food left out beyond safe holding time.
servingSuggestions: Serve with rice, ssam greens, scallion salad, and a reviewed ssamjang.
Provide a small bone plate and make bones visible to children and guests.

faq.question: What makes the cut “LA-style”?
faq.answer: The ribs are cut flanken-style across several bones into thin strips. Multiple origin explanations circulate, so this draft does not present one as definitive.

faq.question: Should I rinse away bone fragments?
faq.answer: No. Ask the butcher to remove bone dust and wipe visible loose fragments with a clean damp disposable towel; rinsing raw beef can spread contamination around the sink.
